title: Trace-one Noetherian invariant finiteness
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let a finite group $G$ act on $R$ by ring automorphisms, and put $A=R^G=\{r\in R:g(r)=r\text{ for all }g\in G\}$. Suppose there exists $a\in R$ with $\sum_{g\in G}g(a)=1$. Then $A$ is Noetherian and $R$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The action need not be faithful, and neither invertibility of $|G|$ in $R$ nor an algebra of finite type over a base ring is assumed.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(b), printed p.75, finite tame strict-local invariant quotient: agent-supplied algebraic finiteness input, in the more general trace-one form. The skew-group idempotent proof is written in report.md; this formulation is not claimed to be a theorem explicitly stated in ILO.

proof.text: Construct the skew group ring $S=\bigoplus_{g\in G}R[g]$ with componentwise addition and $(r[g])(s[h])=r g(s)[gh]$. Its unit is $1[1]$; associativity follows on basis terms because both bracketings of $(r[g])(s[h])(u[k])$ equal $r g(s)(gh)(u)[ghk]$, and hence follows for sums by distributivity. Embed $R$ by $r\mapsto r[1]$. As a RIGHT $R$-module, $S$ is finite free on the $[g]$: the identity $r[g]=[g]g^{-1}(r)$ gives spanning and uniqueness follows by comparing the original coefficients. Regard this as a left $R$-module by $r\cdot s=sr$, which is permitted since $R$ is commutative. In particular it is finite in the sense of [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Exposé VI 3.7(b), printed p.75: motivating finite invariant quotient; agent-written trace-one algebraic argument, expanded from coord/reports/Q94/lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient.md, Algebraic arguments, second argument.

proof.text: Put $e=\sum_{g\in G}g(a)[g]\in S$. For each $h\in G$, reindexing $g\mapsto hg$ gives $[h]e=e$. Therefore $e^2=\sum_g g(a)[g]e=(\sum_g g(a))e=e$. The coefficient-sum map $\pi:S\to R$, $\pi(\sum r_g[g])=\sum r_g$, satisfies $\pi(re)=r\sum_g g(a)=r$. Thus $r\mapsto re$ is injective. Also $(\sum r_g[g])e=(\sum r_g)e$, so $Se=Re$. These are direct calculations using precisely the assumed trace-one identity, with no division by $|G|$.

source.place: Exposé VI 3.7(b), printed p.75: motivating finite invariant quotient; agent-written trace-one algebraic argument, expanded from coord/reports/Q94/lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient.md, Algebraic arguments, second argument.

proof.text: The corner $C=eSe=\{ese:s\in S\}$ is a ring under the inherited addition and multiplication with unit $e$, by $e^2=e$. Every $c\in C$ is uniquely $re$ since $C\subseteq Se=Re$. Since $[h]c=[h]ese=ese=c$, while $[h]re=h(r)e$, injectivity of $r\mapsto re$ gives $h(r)=r$ for every $h$, so $r\in A$. Conversely every $b\in A$ commutes with each $[g]$ and with $R$, hence with $e$, and $be=ebe\in C$. Consequently $C=Ae$ and $b\mapsto be$ is a ring isomorphism $A\to C$ (multiplication gives $(be)(b'e)=bb'e$). Moreover $r\mapsto re$ identifies $R$ as an $A$-module with $Se$ as a right $C$-module, because $(re)(be)=rb e$ and $A$ is commutative.

source.place: Exposé VI 3.7(b), printed p.75: motivating finite invariant quotient; agent-written trace-one algebraic argument, expanded from coord/reports/Q94/lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient.md, Algebraic arguments, second argument.

proof.text: Let $I=SeS$ denote the two-sided ideal consisting of finite sums $n s$ with $n\in Se$ and $s\in S$. It is a right $R$-submodule of the finite right $R$-module $S$. Apply [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented] to this submodule using the left $R$-module convention of Step 1: $R$ is commutative Noetherian by hypothesis and $S$ is finite. Thus $I$ has finitely many right $R$-generators $y_j$. Expand each $y_j$ as a finite sum $\sum_k n_{jk}s_{jk}$ with $n_{jk}\in Se$. Collect the finitely many $n_{jk}$ into $n_1,\ldots,n_t$. Then $I=\sum_i n_i S$: the right side is contained in $I$, and it contains every $y_j$ and therefore every right $R$-linear combination of them. This is only a finite-generator extraction from the definition of $SeS$.

source.place: Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation (2), followed by the displayed elementary extraction of generators of SeS.

proof.text: Multiplying the equality of Step 4 on the right by $e$ gives $Se=Ie=\sum_i n_i S e$; here $Ie\subseteq Se$ and $x=xe\in Ie$ for every $x\in Se$. Since $n_i=n_i e$, every summand $n_i s e$ equals $n_i(ese)$. Step 3 writes $ese=be$ for some $b\in A$; write $n_i=r_i e$. For any $r\in R$, express $re=\sum_i n_i s_i e=\sum_i r_i b_i e$ and apply the injectivity from Step 2 to obtain $r=\sum_i r_i b_i$. Thus $r_1,\ldots,r_t$ generate $R$ over $A$, exactly [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Exposé VI 3.7(b), printed p.75: motivating finite invariant quotient; agent-written trace-one algebraic argument, expanded from coord/reports/Q94/lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient.md, Algebraic arguments, second argument.

proof.text: It remains to show $A$ Noetherian. Define $\rho:R\to A$ by $\rho(r)=\sum_g g(ar)$. The sum is invariant by reindexing; $\rho$ is additive and $A$-linear, and $\rho(b)=b$ for $b\in A$ since $\sum_g g(a)=1$. Let $J$ be any ideal of $A$. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], the ideal $JR$ has finitely many generators $f_k$. Expand each $f_k$ as a finite $R$-linear combination of elements of $J$, and collect those finitely many elements as $j_1,\ldots,j_v\in J$. They generate $JR$. For $b\in J$ write $b=\sum_i j_i r_i$ and apply $\rho$ to get $b=\sum_i j_i\rho(r_i)$. Hence the $j_i$ generate $J$ over $A$. Every ideal of $A$ is finitely generated, so $A$ is Noetherian by the same definition.
